chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'We will gradually entice them from where they do not know.'
He said: 'He is the servant who commits a sin, and the Bounty is renewed for him along with it. That Bounty distracts him from seeking forgiveness for that sin.'

key_terms.سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ: We will gradually entice/draw them out

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of istidraj (gradual allurement) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the concept of istidraj by linking divine favor to spiritual neglect; when blessings are renewed immediately after a sin, they act as a veil that distracts the servant from repentance. This interpretation highlights a subtle form of divine punishment where comfort, rather than hardship, leads to deeper heedlessness, a key theme in Shia exegetical tradition regarding the tests of the righteous and the wicked.
